exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 At the Photo Exhibition
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Emma: That exhibition of Bill Cunningham's street photos was wonderful, wasn't it?
Jack: It really was. I love that he photographed ordinary people, not just famous stars.
Emma: Yes. The guide said he rode the same old bicycle around New York for years.
Jack: And he always wore that simple blue jacket. He cared nothing for money.
Emma: My favourite part was that he went out every day, even in the rain.
Jack: Mine too. The photo of a woman on a snowy street felt so alive.
Emma: I think his secret was patience. He waited for the perfect moment.
Jack: Exactly. After today, I really want to try street photography myself.
exercises.translation_cn: Emma 和 Jack 看完 Bill Cunningham 的街拍摄影展;他拍普通人而非明星;骑同一辆旧自行车、总穿蓝外套、不在乎钱;每天出门拍照,即使下雨;Jack 觉得雪天街上女子的照片很生动;Emma 认为他的秘诀是耐心、等待最佳时机;Jack 看完想自己尝试街拍。

options: Ordinary people, not only famous stars.

options: Every day, even in the rain.

exercises.title: U2 听力·独白 The Last Clog Maker
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: In a small town lives one of the last traditional clog makers.
Every morning he chooses a block of soft wood and shapes it slowly by hand.
Making a single pair of wooden shoes can take him a whole day.
He says machines could do it faster, but they could never give each pair its own character.
Few young people want to learn the craft today, because it is hard and pays little.
Still, he keeps a small workshop open and teaches anyone who is truly interested.
He hopes the old skill will not disappear with him.
exercises.translation_cn: 一个小镇上住着最后几位传统木鞋匠之一。他每天清晨挑一块软木,慢慢用手雕成。做一双木鞋要花他一整天。他说机器更快,却给不了每双鞋独特的个性。如今很少有年轻人愿学这门又难又挣钱少的手艺。但他仍开着小作坊,教任何真心想学的人,希望这门老手艺不会随他消失。

questions.stem: What does the man make?

options: Each pair gains its own character.

questions.stem: Why do few young people learn the craft?
options: It can only be done at night.
It is hard and earns little money.

questions.stem: What does he hope for the future?
options: That the skill will not die out.

exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 Interview with a Young Photographer
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Host: Today we're talking with Lily, a young photographer. Lily, how did you start?
Lily: Thank you. I started by simply watching people on the street for hours.
Host: Interesting. So observation came before the camera?
Lily: Yes. My teacher said a photographer must first learn to see.
Host: What do you enjoy photographing most?
Lily: Small everyday moments, like an old man feeding birds in the park.
Host: Do you use expensive equipment?
Lily: Not at all. Light and patience matter far more than a costly camera.
Host: That's wonderful advice. Thank you, Lily.
exercises.translation_cn: 主持人采访年轻摄影师 Lily。她说自己最初是花几小时观察街上的人;观察先于相机;老师说摄影师必须先学会观察;她最爱拍日常小瞬间,比如公园里喂鸟的老人;她不用昂贵器材,认为光线和耐心远比贵相机重要;主持人称赞这是很好的建议。

options: To observe carefully, or to see.

exercises.title: U2 听力·独白 Paper-cutting Comes Back to Life
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Paper-cutting is one of China's oldest folk arts.
For a while, fewer and fewer people practised it, and many feared it would be forgotten.
Recently, however, the art has become popular again.
Schools now invite old artists to teach children how to cut delicate flowers and animals from red paper.
Online videos of skilled artisans have been watched by millions of people.
Many say they enjoy the calm, careful nature of the work in such a busy world.
Thanks to this new interest, an ancient craft is finding fresh life.
exercises.translation_cn: 剪纸是中国最古老的民间艺术之一。曾有一阵子练习的人越来越少,许多人担心它会被遗忘。然而最近这门艺术又流行起来。学校请老艺人教孩子用红纸剪出精致的花鸟;技艺高超的艺人的网络视频被数百万人观看;很多人说在忙碌的世界里喜欢这种平静而专注的工作。多亏这股新兴趣,一门古老手艺正焕发新生。

exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 In the Clock Room
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Guide: Welcome. This room holds some of the oldest clocks in our museum.
Visitor: They're beautiful! Where did they come from?
Guide: Many were gifts to Chinese emperors from foreign envoys long ago.
Visitor: How are such old clocks kept working?
Guide: A few skilled masters repair them, but each one takes months of work.
Visitor: Months? That sounds incredibly slow.
Guide: It must be slow. Every tiny part has to be cleaned and fixed by hand.
Visitor: When a clock chimes, it must feel like magic.
Guide: It does. To the masters, that sound is the finest music in the world.
exercises.translation_cn: 讲解员带访客参观博物馆里最古老的钟表。许多钟是古时外国使节献给中国皇帝的;少数技艺高超的师傅修理它们,但每件要花几个月;访客觉得很慢;讲解员说必须慢,每个小部件都要手工清洁、修复;钟报时时仿佛魔法;对师傅们来说,那声音是世上最美的音乐。

exercises.title: U2 听力·独白 A Tip for Young Photographers
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here is one simple tip for anyone who loves photography or any craft.
Slow down and really look at the world around you.
The best pictures and the finest work do not come from expensive tools, but from patience and a careful eye.
Notice the small things that others walk past: the light on a wall, the lines on an old hand.
If you train yourself to see, ideas will come from everywhere.
Remember, a careful observer today can become a true artist tomorrow.
exercises.translation_cn: 给所有热爱摄影或任何手艺的人一个简单建议:慢下来,真正去看你周围的世界。最好的照片和最精的作品不来自昂贵器材,而来自耐心和细致的眼睛。留意别人匆匆走过的小事:墙上的光、老人手上的纹路。若你训练自己去观察,灵感会来自四面八方。记住,今天细心的观察者,明天可以成为真正的艺术家。

questions.stem: Who is this tip mainly for?
